Guarantee Or Result: Loads are ordered with loads, stores with stores, and stores with older loads; a load may pass an older store to a different address. [1]
Example Or Mapping: Store Buffering with x=0,y=0; each thread stores one variable then loads the other; both loads may return 0. [1]
Caveat: Scope is coherent write-back memory, not I/O or every special memory operation. [1]

Guarantee Or Result: Atomic access is indivisible for its atomic object, but relaxed creates no operation ordering. [2]
Example Or Mapping: GCC 14.2.0, x86-64 default target, -O2: MOV load.
Caveat: This is one compiler build's output, not a required universal lowering.

Guarantee Or Result: Release/acquire can synchronize when the acquire reads from the release sequence headed by the release operation. [2]
Example Or Mapping: GCC 14.2.0, x86-64 default target, -O2: MOV for acquire load and release store.
Caveat: Same instruction as relaxed in this tested build does not erase the distinct C++ compiler-level contract.

Guarantee Or Result: SC operations participate in a single total order under the standard's constraints; the strongest SC guarantee has conditions and weaker operations affect the guarantee. [2]
Example Or Mapping: GCC 14.2.0, x86-64 default target, -O2: SC store emitted XCHG; fetch_add emitted LOCK XADD.
Caveat: Exact lowering varies by compiler and target; LLVM documents an x86 MFENCE lowering for SC fences. [3]

Guarantee Or Result: Locked instructions have a total order and ordinary loads/stores are not reordered with them. [1]
Example Or Mapping: LOCK XADD and LOCK CMPXCHG are representative atomic RMW instructions.
Caveat: Verify instruction, alignment, and memory-type constraints against current vendor manuals before relying on special cases.

Guarantee Or Result: Atomic memory orders constrain code motion and may map to target instructions or fences; the target selects patterns and unsupported lock-free sequences may call runtime support. [4]
Example Or Mapping: Compare emitted assembly from the supplied C++ source using the recorded GCC command.
Caveat: Never treat a C++ memory_order as a one-to-one mnemonic mapping.

Guarantee Or Result: With atomic locations, relaxed C++ permits seeing publication flag=1 with stale payload; x86 write-back memory forbids the corresponding store-store/load-load outcome. [5, 2]
Example Or Mapping: Writer: payload.store(1); ready.store(1). Reader: read ready then payload. Release/acquire on ready synchronizes when acquire reads the release value. [6]
Caveat: The example uses atomic payload to keep relaxed variant defined; release/acquire on publication flag is the portable synchronizing version. [2]

Guarantee Or Result: Opposite read orders (x=1,y=0 versus y=1,x=0) are forbidden on x86 and with all operations seq_cst; the relaxed C++ model permits the split view. [7, 2]
Example Or Mapping: Two writers independently store x=1 and y=1; two readers load x-then-y and y-then-x. [7]
Caveat: Keep all accesses atomic when comparing C++ relaxed behavior; plain racy accesses are not a valid language-level litmus test. [2]
